correction: A sidechain changes what controls a processor; the detector source is not automatically the audio being heard through the processed channel.
myth: external sidechain detection has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: On a duplicated test route, feed a clearly different trigger into Compressor side chain, use Listen to verify the detector where available, then compare bypassed and active processing.

correction: The plug-in header Side Chain menu selects the external detector source; plug-in sidechain controls then shape detection.
myth: selecting a sidechain input in Logic has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Solo a short representative section, choose the intended source from the plug-in Side Chain menu, then verify detector activity before changing threshold or ratio.

correction: Kick/bass ducking is a time-varying level relationship; the useful amount depends on overlap, envelope, tempo, and musical hierarchy.
myth: kick-triggered bass ducking has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Route the kick to the bass compressor sidechain, start with obvious gain reduction to confirm timing, then back off threshold, ratio, attack, and release while level-matching.

correction: Vocal-triggered ducking lowers selected accompaniment only while vocal energy is present; it is not the same as simply making the vocal louder.
myth: vocal-triggered music ducking has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Route the vocal or a filtered vocal bus to a music-bus compressor sidechain, begin with 1–2 dB of audible reduction, and compare in context at matched vocal loudness.

correction: Audible pumping is created by the detector rhythm and compressor recovery envelope, not by sidechain routing alone.
myth: rhythmic pumping has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Use a simple four-on-the-floor trigger or ghost kick, exaggerate threshold and ratio, then tune attack and release against one bar before reducing depth.

correction: A ghost trigger is a non-audible rhythmic control source used only by the detector; it should remain clearly separated from the audible mix path.
myth: ghost-trigger sidechain has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Create a muted/no-output MIDI or audio trigger routed to a bus visible to the sidechain, verify the bus meter and detector, then compare with the trigger disabled.

correction: Filtering the detector changes what causes gain reduction without directly EQing the target audio.
myth: sidechain filtering has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Enable the Compressor sidechain filter and Listen, sweep frequency/Q to isolate the useful trigger component, then disable Listen and compare gain-reduction behavior.

correction: No gain reduction can result from source selection, silent routing, threshold, detector filtering, plug-in position, or source timing—not only a broken compressor.
myth: sidechain compressor not reacting has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Temporarily lower threshold and raise ratio, verify the selected sidechain source and meter, use Side Chain Listen where available, then restore musical settings.

correction: A gate sidechain uses one signal to open or close another path; it is useful for keyed effects but can truncate natural attacks or tails.
myth: noise-gate sidechaining has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Select a clear trigger as Noise Gate sidechain, exaggerate threshold/range to verify the relationship, then tune attack, hold, and release on one phrase.

correction: Stereo detection mode, lookahead, routing latency, and trigger timing can change when and how both channels duck.
myth: stereo, latency, and sidechain timing has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Use a simple centered trigger, compare detector Sum/Max and Peak/RMS choices, bypass latency-heavy upstream plug-ins, and inspect whether both channels recover together.

correction: Track automation belongs to the timeline/track; region automation belongs to the region and can move or loop with it.
myth: track versus region automation has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Duplicate a short region, place one test move as track automation and one as region automation, then move/loop the region and observe which data follows.

correction: A short word or phrase ride is a deliberate level change over time, distinct from changing the whole region or increasing compression.
myth: word-level volume rides has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Show volume automation, add boundary points around the word, move the enclosed segment slightly, and compare the phrase in context.

correction: Pan automation changes spatial position over time; on stereo material Balance and Stereo Pan can represent different operations.
myth: pan automation has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Automate one modest left-to-right move over a duplicated section, use a smooth curve, then check speakers, headphones, and mono.

correction: Any exposed automatable plug-in parameter can have its own lane, but the parameter must be selected and the plug-in state must remain compatible.
myth: plug-in parameter automation has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Choose the target plug-in parameter in the automation lane, place a small two-state move, and compare with the lane bypassed/read off.

correction: Automating a send changes how much source enters a parallel effect; automating the return changes every source using that effect.
myth: send automation has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Select the source Send Level automation lane, add points around one phrase, raise it modestly, and compare against automating the aux return.

correction: A throw is a short, intentional increase in effect feed or return at a specific lyric or transition, with tail behavior preserved.
myth: reverb and delay throws has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Automate the send around the target word, start the rise just before the word ends, return the send after it, and leave the aux tail unmuted.

correction: A filter sweep changes cutoff/resonance over time; the perceived build also depends on source spectrum, level, and resonance.
myth: filter-sweep automation has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Automate cutoff over the buildup with two boundary points, keep resonance modest, and level-match the end state against bypass.

correction: Automation points define values at times; curve shape determines how the parameter travels between them.
myth: automation points and curves has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Create two fixed endpoint points, add a midpoint only if needed, compare linear and curved movement, and keep the simplest shape that matches the phrase.

correction: Whether automation follows a moved/copied region depends on ownership and project settings; copied data can create hidden duplicates.
myth: moving and copying automation with musical material has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: On a Project Alternative, copy one region with its automation option enabled/disabled, inspect both Track and Region lanes, then keep the behavior that matches the arrangement.

correction: The same numeric automation move can sound different before/after compression, on a source versus bus, or on a send versus return.
myth: automation scope and processing order has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Compare a small source-volume ride, pre-compressor gain move, bus ride, and send move on duplicated settings, changing only one stage at a time.

correction: Read plays existing automation and returns controls to the written curve; manual moves are temporary unless another write mode is used.
myth: Read automation mode has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Switch the track to Read, reveal the active parameter lane, locate the written values, and compare playback with automation temporarily Off.

correction: Touch writes while the control is touched, then returns to existing automation after release.
myth: Touch automation mode has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Duplicate the project section, choose Touch, move the fader through one phrase, release early, and inspect the return/ramp behavior.

correction: Latch begins writing when touched and continues at the last value after release until playback stops or mode changes.
myth: Latch automation mode has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Use Latch on a duplicate section, touch the control at the intended change, release it, stop after the section, and inspect the written plateau.

correction: Write continuously replaces automation as the playhead passes and can erase existing data even when a control is not actively moved.
myth: Write automation mode has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: On a disposable Project Alternative only, observe Write across a tiny blank test lane, then return all production tracks to Read/Touch before real work.

correction: Trim offsets existing volume/pan/send automation; Relative adds an offset curve while preserving the primary curve.
myth: Trim and Relative automation has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Duplicate the track, compare a small Trim Touch offset against a Relative curve over the same range, then inspect both primary and offset data.

correction: A control snaps back when Read automation, a different automation owner, controller data, or plug-in modulation reasserts its stored value.
myth: controls snapping back to automated values has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Reveal the exact parameter automation, toggle Track/Region view and automation Off, then disable external controller input one source at a time.

correction: Sudden jumps usually indicate discontinuous points, Latch/Write data, relative offsets, copied automation, or a different owner becoming active.
myth: unexpected automation jumps has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Zoom into the jump, inspect all visible and relative lanes plus region automation, then bypass one owner and adjust the smallest pair of points.

correction: Recovery depends on stopping writes immediately, using Undo/Project Alternatives, and preserving the current state before further playback.
myth: recovering overwritten automation has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Stop playback, switch affected tracks to Read, save a new Project Alternative, inspect Undo History, and compare any duplicate/backup automation before editing.

correction: Automation can exist on multiple parameters and owners; deleting the visible lane alone may leave other data active.
myth: deleting or resetting automation has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Select the exact parameter and Track/Region owner, save a Project Alternative, delete the bounded range, then play through with automation Read.

correction: Touch, Latch, or Write can record fader/knob/controller movements during playback or recording; mode and parameter selection determine what is written.
myth: recording live automation has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Select one parameter, choose Touch, loop a short section, perform one pass, then inspect and simplify the resulting points before a second pass.

correction: Automation preferences such as ramp time and mode behavior affect how controls return and how much data is written.
myth: automation-mode safety and return settings has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Use a duplicate project, adjust one relevant automation preference, record the same short Touch move, and compare return shape and point density.

correction: The quantize value defines the target grid; choosing the wrong subdivision can move correct notes to the wrong musical locations.
myth: note-value quantization has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Duplicate the MIDI region, select a short phrase, compare the smallest plausible straight/swing/tuplet grids at reduced Q-Strength, and listen with the groove source.

correction: Region quantization affects the region non-destructively as a whole; Piano Roll note operations can target selected events directly.
myth: region versus note quantization has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Duplicate the region, apply Region inspector quantization to one copy and selected-note Piano Roll quantization to another, then compare editable state and result.

correction: Q-Strength determines how far eligible notes move toward the grid; it changes correction amount, not which notes qualify.
myth: Q-Strength has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Set a correct grid, compare 100% against a moderate Q-Strength on a duplicated two-bar phrase, and level-match the instrument playback.

correction: Q-Range decides which notes are eligible based on distance from grid; Q-Strength decides how far eligible notes move.
myth: Q-Range has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Choose the intended grid, start Q-Range near zero, move it positive until already-good notes stop changing, then set Q-Strength for remaining outliers.

correction: Q-Swing offsets alternating grid positions; swing feel depends on subdivision, source groove, tempo, and existing timing.
myth: Q-Swing and swing quantization has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Duplicate two bars, select the correct base subdivision, raise Q-Swing gradually from straight, and compare with kick/snare/bass in context.

correction: A groove template derives a quantize grid from source note/transient timing; it transfers timing references, not the source’s full musical expression.
myth: groove templates has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Create a groove template from a clean two-bar reference, apply it at reduced strength to a duplicated support region, and compare against the source.

correction: Quantization need not affect every note; selection, Q-Range, and separate regions can isolate mistakes.
myth: partial and selected-note quantization has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: In Piano Roll, select only the clearly late/early notes, audition before/after one by one, and quantize them at partial strength to the intended grid.

correction: Musical feel can come from consistent relation to the beat; visual distance from grid is not automatically an error.
myth: intentional ahead/behind-the-beat timing has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Compare the part against kick/snare/bass, measure several repeated events, and correct only inconsistent deviations while leaving the coherent offset.

correction: Groove damage often comes from wrong grid, excessive strength, broad eligibility, overlapping quantization layers, or loss of intentional offsets.
myth: quantization ruining the groove has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Turn Region Quantize Off on a duplicate, compare grid, Q-Strength, Q-Range, Q-Swing, and selected-note edits one variable at a time.

correction: Tuplets, mixed quantize values, grace notes, flams, and rolled chords require grids or selections that represent their actual musical structure.
myth: mixed, tuplets, and non-straight rhythms has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Isolate one ornament/tuplet group, compare the proper tuplet or mixed grid at reduced strength, and leave decorative notes unquantized if the grid cannot represent them.

correction: Moving note starts can create overlaps, gaps, or pedal conflicts; timing correction must be checked against note ends and instrument articulation.
myth: note length and overlap after quantization has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: After quantizing a duplicated phrase, inspect note ends and sustain-pedal data, then adjust Q-Length or selected lengths only where the instrument audibly changes.

correction: Velocity is event data interpreted by the instrument; it may control loudness, timbre, articulation, sample layer, or several parameters.
myth: MIDI velocity and instrument response has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Play or edit one repeated note across low, medium, and high velocities, then listen for level, timbre, attack, and articulation changes.

correction: Individual velocity edits can fix isolated accents without changing timing or every note in the phrase.
myth: editing individual note velocities has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Select one offending note, adjust velocity while looping the phrase, and compare it against neighboring notes at the same musical role.

correction: Scaling multiplies the velocity pattern, preserving proportions more than setting every note to a fixed value.
myth: scaling velocities has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Duplicate the region, scale all velocities modestly up/down, and compare timbre, loudness, and sample-layer changes with track level matched.

correction: Velocity compression narrows differences; expansion increases differences around a pivot. Neither is audio compression.
myth: compressing or expanding velocity range has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: On a duplicate region, apply modest velocity compression/expansion, inspect minimum/maximum values, and compare repeated roles rather than peak loudness.

correction: A crescendo is a shaped change across notes; its musical effect depends on instrument response, phrase timing, and orchestration.
myth: MIDI crescendos and diminuendos has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Select the phrase, draw or transform a velocity crescendo from a realistic start/end range, then listen for timbre as well as loudness.

correction: Random velocity adds variation, not musical intent; useful ranges must be bounded around a coherent accent pattern.
myth: velocity randomization has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Duplicate two bars, mark intentional accents, randomize only non-accent notes within a small range, and compare repeated loops.

correction: Accents define rhythmic and phrase hierarchy; matching all velocities removes information about meter, groove, and emphasis.
myth: accent hierarchy has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Select repeated roles, set clear anchor accents first, then adjust intermediate notes relative to those anchors while looping in context.

correction: Changing velocities between verse and chorus can alter both loudness and timbre, but section impact also depends on arrangement and register.
myth: section-level velocity contrast has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Duplicate representative verse/chorus regions, scale chorus velocities modestly, level-match playback, and judge timbre/attack against arrangement changes.

correction: Consistency means stable role hierarchy and controlled outliers, not one fixed velocity for every drum hit.
myth: consistent drums without identical hits has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Separate kick/snare/hat roles, compress each velocity range modestly, preserve anchor accents, and compare several loop repetitions.

correction: Many instruments map velocity to different samples, filters, attacks, or articulations, so velocity changes can alter tone more than level.
myth: velocity-sensitive instruments and sample layers has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Test a small set of repeated notes across the relevant velocity range, identify sample/articulation transitions, then constrain edits around the desired zone.

correction: Matching velocities can correct accidental outliers, but equal numbers do not guarantee equal perceived loudness across pitch, sample, or articulation.
myth: matching and normalizing selected velocities has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Select same-role notes, set or scale them toward a common range, then audition across pitches and adjust perceptual outliers manually.

correction: Velocity is fixed at note-on for most instruments; expression/volume can shape a note after it begins.
myth: velocity versus expression and volume has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Hold one long note, compare changing velocity at note-on against Expression/CC or volume automation during the sustain, and keep the controller that matches the musical intent.

correction: MIDI Transform selects events by conditions and applies defined operations in bulk; selection and operation are separate stages.
myth: MIDI Transform workflow has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: On a duplicated region, open MIDI Transform, set a narrow selection condition, use Select Only first, verify highlighted events, then Apply Operation.

correction: Pitch conditions let MIDI Transform target one note or range, useful for drum lanes or register-specific edits.
myth: selecting notes by pitch has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Duplicate the region, set pitch Equal/Inside range, choose Select Only, verify every highlighted note, then apply a small operation.

correction: Velocity conditions can isolate quiet, loud, or outlier notes before a targeted transformation.
myth: selecting notes by velocity has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Use Velocity Inside/Below/Above selection, run Select Only, audition the selected role, then scale or add a small amount.

correction: MIDI channel conditions can isolate events in multichannel regions, but channel assignments may encode articulations or external routing.
myth: selecting MIDI by channel has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Inspect Event List channel values, use MIDI Transform Channel condition with Select Only, then apply a harmless test before the real operation.

correction: Logic Humanize randomizes position, velocity, and length within ranges; it does not understand groove, accents, phrasing, or instrument role.
myth: Humanize transform has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Duplicate two bars, protect anchor notes/accents, apply very small Humanize ranges, and compare repeated loops against the original and groove reference.

correction: Random timing offsets create noise around current positions; they do not create a coherent ahead/behind pocket.
myth: small timing randomization has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Select only secondary repeated notes, randomize position within a very small range, and compare against the same loop over multiple repetitions.

correction: Fixed-length transforms set selected note durations uniformly; this can be useful for gates or triggers but destroys articulation variation.
myth: fixed note lengths has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Duplicate the region, select the target pitch/channel, apply a fixed length, then inspect overlaps and compare articulation with the original.

correction: Transposition changes pitch values while preserving timing/velocity unless another operation is included; range and instrument limits still matter.
myth: batch transposition has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Use pitch/channel conditions and Select Only, transpose a duplicated phrase by the intended interval, then check range, harmony, and articulation triggers.

correction: Add, scale, compress, expand, crescendo, and fixed-velocity operations produce different relationships among selected values.
myth: batch velocity transformations has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: On a duplicate, Select Only the target role, compare Add versus Scale or Compress/Expand with modest settings, and inspect limits/sample changes.

correction: Custom Transform sets make repeated operations reproducible, but stale conditions can silently affect the wrong events in another region.
myth: saved MIDI Transform sets has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Create a named custom Transform set, reopen it on a duplicate region, use Select Only, compare conditions, then apply and undo once.

correction: Transform operations act on the current selected/defined events; safe use requires a duplicate, verified scope, and immediate result inspection.
myth: MIDI Transform scope and undo has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Duplicate the region or Project Alternative, run Select Only, screenshot/note conditions, Apply once, inspect Event List differences, and test Undo before continuing.

correction: Humanize adds bounded randomness; a groove template transfers a coherent timing reference from a performance.
myth: Humanize versus groove template has one universally correct setting or workflow.
safer_principle: Preserve a baseline, establish the correct owner/scope, and use one bounded experiment: Duplicate the region, apply tiny Humanize to one copy and a reduced-strength groove template to another, then compare against the rhythm section.

correction: A sidechain normally controls detection; it is not automatically mixed into the target output.
myth: Sidechain audio is always audible in the processed channel.
safer_principle: Establish the actual Logic owner, detector, event set, and musical role before changing data; preserve an undoable baseline.

correction: External detection also supports subtle unmasking, dialogue/vocal ducking, keyed gates, and detector control.
myth: Sidechain compression is only for EDM pumping.
safer_principle: Establish the actual Logic owner, detector, event set, and musical role before changing data; preserve an undoable baseline.

correction: First verify source selection, routing, detector filtering, timing, and whether the trigger actually reaches the plug-in.
myth: If the compressor is not reacting, lower the threshold forever.
safer_principle: Establish the actual Logic owner, detector, event set, and musical role before changing data; preserve an undoable baseline.

correction: Write can erase existing automation as playback passes; Touch or Latch is usually safer for ordinary passes.
myth: Write mode is the normal safe way to ride a fader.
safer_principle: Establish the actual Logic owner, detector, event set, and musical role before changing data; preserve an undoable baseline.

correction: Read automation or another data owner is usually reasserting a stored value.
myth: A fader that snaps back is broken.
safer_principle: Establish the actual Logic owner, detector, event set, and musical role before changing data; preserve an undoable baseline.

correction: They have different ownership and move/loop behavior.
myth: Region and track automation are interchangeable.
safer_principle: Establish the actual Logic owner, detector, event set, and musical role before changing data; preserve an undoable baseline.

correction: Grid, strength, range, swing, selection, and groove templates independently shape the result.
myth: Quantize always means 100 percent to the nearest grid.
safer_principle: Establish the actual Logic owner, detector, event set, and musical role before changing data; preserve an undoable baseline.

correction: Randomness adds variance, not coherent pocket, phrasing, or hierarchy.
myth: Random timing automatically creates human feel.
safer_principle: Establish the actual Logic owner, detector, event set, and musical role before changing data; preserve an undoable baseline.

correction: Instrument response varies by pitch, sample layer, articulation, and mapping.
myth: Equal MIDI velocities produce equal perceived loudness.
safer_principle: Establish the actual Logic owner, detector, event set, and musical role before changing data; preserve an undoable baseline.

correction: Velocity is note-on data interpreted by the instrument and often changes timbre or articulation.
myth: Velocity is the same as track volume.
safer_principle: Establish the actual Logic owner, detector, event set, and musical role before changing data; preserve an undoable baseline.

correction: The transform applies bounded random changes; musical hierarchy must be designed separately.
myth: Humanize understands which notes should be accented.
safer_principle: Establish the actual Logic owner, detector, event set, and musical role before changing data; preserve an undoable baseline.

correction: Use Select Only and verify the event set before applying an operation.
myth: MIDI Transform should be applied before checking selection conditions.
safer_principle: Establish the actual Logic owner, detector, event set, and musical role before changing data; preserve an undoable baseline.
